Compensation Range:

Hourly: $26.63 - $28.89

National University – San Diego, California


Part-time Faculty: Inspired Teaching and Learning


Location: Remote, USA


National University is a veteran-founded, San Diego-based nonprofit. Since 1971, our mission has been to provide accessible higher education to adult learners. Today, we educate a diverse student body from across the U.S. and around the globe, with more than 230,000 alumni worldwide. Our three schools and three colleges offer more than 200 accredited and licensed graduate and undergraduate programs. National University holds accreditation through the Western Senior College and Universities Commission (WSCUC).


Position Summary

The Department of Teacher Education, in the Sanford College of Education at the National University invites applications for part-time faculty in Inspired Teaching and Learning. The successful candidate will have a demonstrated record of or potential for excellence in teaching in their field and a commitment to serving the university’s diverse adult student body. The successful candidate will have the potential for a commitment to serving the university’s diverse adult student body. This position primarily works closely with the Academic Program Director and other faculty within the program and contributes to ensuring program quality, student engagement, and success.


Essential Job Duties:

  • Provide substantive, timely feedback to students on various assessment activities.
  • Maintain a positive, safe, inclusive student-centric learning environment.
  • Complete required tasks on deadlines (e.g., final grades, assessment, grading rubrics, input for grade appeals, etc.)
  • Maintain appropriate professional training and/or scholarly activities, when applicable.
  • Provide feedback to the course lead regarding the course content.
  • Identify at-risk students and collaborate with student services.

Qualifications:

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum master's degree in education or a closely related field from a regionally accredited institution.
  • Current and active California Single Subject Teaching Credential.
  • Knowledge of California frameworks, standards, assessment systems, and current educational initiatives.
  • 5+ years of secondary (grades 6-12) classroom teaching experience in a Single Subject area (e.g., Art, English, Mathematics, Science, Social Science, World Languages, Physical Education, Theatre, etc.).
  • 3+ years (within the past 5 years) of secondary classroom teaching demonstrating current knowledge of instructional practices, student engagement strategies, curriculum standards, and assessment practices.
  • Experience mentoring, coaching, supervising, or supporting teacher candidates, beginning teachers, or interns.
  • Higher education teaching experience in teacher preparation, particularly in methods, clinical practice, supervision, or field experience courses.
  • Experience using data to improve instruction and candidate performance.
  • Knowledge of teacher performance assessments (CalTPA or similar).
  • Experience supporting diverse student populations including English learners and students with disabilities.
  • Experience working with adult learners and facilitating professional learning for educators.
  • Demonstrated proficiency with instructional technology and educational AI tools including the ability to model responsible, ethical, and effective integration into teaching and learning.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience serving in teacher leadership roles such as department chair, instructional coach, mentor teacher, PLC leader, curriculum leader, grade-level lead, or similar positions.
  • Experience collaborating with schools, districts, and community partners to support teacher preparation.

For full consideration, interested candidates should provide the following:

  • A cover letter.
  • A curriculum vita.
  • Statement of teaching experience online and/or onsite for a diverse student body.
  • Unofficial transcripts of highest degree attained.

Candidate receiving offers will be offered a salary/pay rate commensurate with experience that vary based on a candidate’s qualifications, skills, and competencies. Absent exceptional circumstances, candidates will be offered a salary within this range for this position. Base pay is one component of National University’s total rewards package, as we are dedicated to supporting the needs of the “whole you” with our holistic approach to employee benefits by offering comprehensive well-being benefits for you and your family. For full details about our benefit plan offerings, please visit . For part-time positions, please click here.

National University is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against any employee or applicant per applicable federal, state and local laws. At NU, a mix of highly talented, innovative, and creative people come together to make the impact of a lifetime for each of our student learners. All qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment, education, and admission at National University.

Construction Assistant

About the Opportunity

Latino Legends is excited to partner with a fast-growing U.S. real estate development and property firm to find a driven Construction Assistant to join their team.

Our client specializes in residential rehabs and new home construction. They are looking for an exceptionally organized, self-directed individual who can own administrative and operational workflows remotely, keep external contractors accountable, and ensure projects move from start to finish without delay.

Position Summary

As the Construction Assistant, you will serve as the operational backbone for active rehab and new build projects. You will manage vendor bidding, permit applications, inspection tracking, contractor compliance, and documentation. This role requires high-volume communication—including extended periods of phone outreach—and meticulous record-keeping to keep projects on schedule and within scope.

Core Responsibilities

  • Rehab Project Coordination:

    • Source and obtain 2–3 competitive bids per project.

    • Collaborate with the Construction Manager to draft detailed Scopes of Work (SOWs) for Requests for Proposals (RFPs).

    • Collect and verify contractor documentation, including licenses, Certificates of Insurance (COI), and W-9s.

    • Administer agreements, handle scope sign-offs, and request vendor invoices.

    • Organize and maintain all project files in Google Drive and Coda.

  • New Home Construction Support:

    • Input and update new build data within Rent Manager.

    • Verify installer COIs and W-9s, request invoices, and finalize contract signatures.

    • Apply for required installation, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, and building permits.

    • Track permit approvals, coordinate on-site inspections, and secure Certificates of Occupancy (CO).

    • Confirm completed job milestones and archive all invoices and Manufacturer Certificates of Origin (MCOs).

  • Contractor Oversight & Administrative Tracking:

    • Conduct persistent phone outreach to confirm job timelines and keep field contractors accountable.

    • Maintain meticulous records to ensure no documentation or compliance step falls through the cracks.

    • Keep project leads proactively updated on project milestones and potential bottlenecks.

Ideal Candidate Profile & Qualifications

  • Experience: 1–2+ years of administrative, operations, or project coordination experience. Prior exposure to construction, real estate, or property management is a plus, but character and work ethic matter most.

  • Mindset & Grit: Resolute, proactive, and solutions-oriented with the stamina to handle back-to-back phone calls and follow-ups.

  • Communication: Exceptional written and spoken English skills with strong interpersonal instincts and professional composure.

  • Organization: High level of autonomy with proven ability to manage complex file systems, schedules, and compliance steps without needing constant reminders.

  • Tech Proficiency: Comfortable working with cloud tools such as Google Drive, Coda, and property management software (experience with Rent Manager is a bonus).

raw.description:
Thriveworks Counseling is seeking individuals pursuing Michigan State Licensure as a LMSW in Michigan to provide telehealth sessions.


About the job
Thriveworks is a mental health care company founded by clinicians in 2008 and still led by them today. With 340+ locations and a nationwide hybrid care model, we serve over 175,000 clients annually through more than 1.7 million sessions, and we're growing. In addition to working directly with clients, we partner with health systems and primary care providers because we believe mental health is inseparable from physical health. As a clinician-led organization, we're built to support the people who do this work with the tools, community, and stability you need to build a career that lasts.

About the Role
We’re hiring licensed clinicians to provide compassionate, evidence-based care to our more than 175,000 clients across the country. You may be a good fit for this role if you’re:

  • Approved by the board as a LLMSW
  • Must be seeking independent licensure and living in Michigan
  • A graduate of an approved 60-credit hour program
  • Graduate or Post-graduate work experience in a counseling setting treating depression and anxiety is required
  • Graduate or Post-graduate work experience independently conducting intakes and diagnosing (preferred) according to the current DSM-5 under a licensed supervisor.
  • Consistently available to clients for a minimum of 25 sessions with 30 hours of availability weekly
  • A behavioral health generalist who is open to treating a variety of clients, including couples and children
  • Invested in helping your clients achieve measurable progress
  • Confident working with modern clinical technology, including telehealth and EHR tools
  • A good teammate — we’re building a clinical community and value positive contributors

Compensation
Up to $62,200 based on licensure type, session volume, and bonus opportunities. Full-time clinicians are eligible for health insurance, student loan repayment assistance, paid time off, and other employer-sponsored benefits.

How We Support You
We handle the administrative work so you can focus on what you do best: providing exceptional care. That means credentialing, billing, scheduling, and marketing support taken care of for you, plus paid orientation and training to get you started. You'll build a full caseload within 90 days of credentialing, with flexible scheduling available seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. ET.

Benefits
As a W2 employee, you'll be eligible to receive:

  • Guaranteed bi-weekly pay for completed sessions
  • FREE group and individual clinical supervision provided
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • 401(k) with employer matching
  • Paid time off
  • Short- and long-term disability insurance
  • Company-paid life and AD&D insurance
  • CEU reimbursement and free in-house training
  • Student loan repayment assistance

Our Community
Being a clinician can feel isolating, especially in a telehealth world. We're built to make sure it doesn't. You'll have access to live clinical support, monthly case consultations, and a vibrant online and in-person community of more than 2,700 licensed providers. All clinical leadership is promoted from within, so the people supporting you have been exactly where you are.

Ready to Join Us?
Apply today to become part of a team that’s changing mental health care for clients and clinicians alike.


Interested in joining Team Thriveworks? We're thrilled to meet you!


With Job scams becoming more and more frequent, here's how to know you're speaking with a real member of our team:

  • Our recruiters and other team members will only email you from or an @thriveworks.com email address.
  • Our recruiters and other team members may also contact you via text or phone to schedule an interview.
  • A google meets interview invitation will be sent via email and will only come from an @thriveworks.com email address.
  • Our interviews will take place over Google Meet (not Microsoft Teams, Zoom, or any other platform).
  • We will never ask you to purchase or send us equipment.

If you see a scam related to Thriveworks, please report it to . You can contact with any questions or concerns.


Thriveworks is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Our people are our most valuable assets. We embrace and encourage differences in age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, national origin, physical and mental ability, race, religion, sexual orientation, veteran status, and other characteristics that make our employees unique. We encourage and welcome diverse candidates to apply for any position you are qualified for to bring your unique perspective to our team.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire. This position is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship, either now or in the future.

raw.description:
Morgan Stanley is a leading global financial services firm providing a wide range of investment banking, securities, investment management and wealth management services. The Firm's employees serve clients worldwide including corporations, governments and individuals from more than 1,200 offices in 43 countries.

As a market leader, the talent and passion of our people is critical to our success. Together, we share a common set of values rooted in integrity, excellence and strong team ethic. Morgan Stanley can provide a superior foundation for building a professional career - a place for people to learn, to achieve and grow. A philosophy that balances personal lifestyles, perspectives and needs is an important part of our culture.

Department Profile:
The Fixed Income Division (“FID”) sits within the Institutional Securities Group (“ISG”) and is comprised of Interest Rate and Currency Products, Credit Products, Commodities, Repo, and TBAs and Distribution. Professionals in FID assess and actively manage risk, trade securities, and structure as well as execute innovative transactions in the fast-paced and constantly changing global markets.

From the largest global institutions to innovative new hedge funds, investors come to Morgan Stanley for sales, trading, and market-making services in almost every type of financial instrument including stocks, bonds, derivatives, foreign exchange, and commodities. Our professionals provide liquidity and content to clients around the world, actively assessing and managing risk, trading securities, and planning and executing transactions in the fast-changing markets. As the needs of our clients become increasingly complex, we often develop customized solutions.

Team Profile:
The Institutional Securities Documentation team sits within FID’s Business Control Unit (“BCU”) and is a first line team comprised of Non-Market Risk (Operational Risk), Counterparty Risk, Conduct Risk and Contract Negotiations. The Institutional Securities Documentation Team covers the contract negotiation function for trading agreements for FID.

We are looking for an individual in the documentation unit supporting the Commodities desks with negotiations of physical and financial master agreements and ancillary documents. As a member of the documentation unit, the team member will review and negotiate ISDA schedules, various ISDA annexes, NAESBs, EEIs, credit support annexes, bespoke physical master agreements, guaranties and ancillary documents. The candidate will work closely with business professionals across the firm, as well as with external counsel and clients. The primary objective will be to execute master agreements in an effective and efficient manor.

RESPONSIBILITIES AND QUALIFICATIONS

Responsibilities include:

  • The timely, consistent and effective negotiation, review, and drafting of master agreements (using both English and New York law) upon request from the Business Unit to help facilitate their business.
  • Liaise with Credit, Risk, Legal, Sales, Operations, Tax and other internal groups to ensure that the appropriate terms are included in all agreements for the effective protection of Morgan Stanley in line with applicable policies, procedures, and regulations.
  • Converse with clients regarding Morgan Stanley’s position in master agreements
  • Keeping work in progress records up to date.
  • Keeping informed of business and regulatory developments as they impact on the way in which the business operates

Qualifications:

  • JD preferred
  • Experience in reviewing, drafting and negotiating the ISDA Master Agreement and other trading documentation preferred
  • College degree required
  • Must have excellent verbal and written skills
  • Strong analytical and organizational skills
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills; the ability to clearly articulate ideas and forge strong relationships internally and with external clients
  • Highly motivated and adaptable; the ability to work on a team of diverse individuals
  • Must be mature and professional
  • Must be proactive and have the ability to work independently and to perform consistently and respond creatively in a high volume fast paced and changing environment
  • Accurate and detail-oriented with sound judgment and integrity

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT FROM MORGAN STANLEY:

At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work.

To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste into your browser.

Expected base pay rates for the role will be between $100,000 and $150,000 per year for Associate at the commencement of employment. However, base pay if hired will be determined on an individualized basis and is only part of the total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, incentive compensation, discretionary bonuses, other short and long-term incentive packages, and other Morgan Stanley sponsored benefit programs.

Morgan Stanley is an equal opportunity employer committed to building and maintaining a workforce that is diverse in experience and background. Our recruiting efforts reflect our strong commitment to a culture of inclusion, where individuals are hired, developed, and advanced based on their skills and talents.

By uniting Aura and Qoria, organizations driven by personal experiences with identity theft and cyberbullying, our combined company brings together global category leaders to create a safer internet for everyone across all stages of life. As Aura expands, we are seeking a creative, results-driven Social Media Specialist & Content Creator to support our content and social strategy. This is a PART-TIME (approximately 30 hours per week) CONTRACT role and must be based in the US (Eastern Timezone preferred).

This role will help make organic social a meaningful awareness engine for Aura by creating engaging, platform-native content that expands our reach, drives conversation, and builds cultural relevance. The ideal candidate is a socially native storyteller who understands what captures attention online, who eagerly looks for new AI tools to implement, and is excited to turn ideas, trends, and audience insights into content people want to watch and share.

What you'll do:

  • Create social-first content: Appear on camera regularly across short-form video, Stories, and other organic formats, bringing scripts and briefs to life with confident, authentic delivery. This is the core of the role.
  • Support content production: Help concept, film, and edit content alongside your on-camera work, and publish across formats including static posts and carousels.
  • Bring creative ideas to life: Turn briefs, trends, audience insights, and cultural moments into compelling content for TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, and other relevant platforms.
  • Support Aura’s organic social channels: Help manage the day-to-day content calendar, including scheduling, publishing, quality assurance, and coordinating assets, while also pulling performance metrics for the team to analyze.
  • Spot trends and move quickly: Stay current on emerging formats, conversations, and platform behaviors, identifying opportunities for Aura to participate in timely and relevant ways.

  • Use AI thoughtfully: Explore AI-powered tools that can accelerate ideation, production, editing, and audience research while maintaining strong creative judgment and brand standards.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally: Partner with social, brand, design, product marketing, and paid media teams to support campaigns and broader business priorities.

What you'll bring:

  • 1–3 years of experience in social media and content creation, including internships, freelance work, or experience building your own channels.
  • Comfort on camera (required): You're confident and natural on screen, and excited to be a regular, recognizable presence across Aura's social channels — this is the core of the role.
  • AI fluency: Experience using AI-powered tools to support content ideation, writing, editing, production, and data collection, plus the creative judgment to use them thoughtfully and responsibly.
  • A genuinely social-native perspective: You understand the culture, trends, and mechanics of platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube.
  • Nice to have — production skills: Comfort filming and editing short-form video using tools such as CapCut, Edits, Canva, or similar. Not required (production support is available).
  • Nice to have — writing instincts: Ability to write clear, engaging hooks, captions, or scripts.
  • Curiosity and adaptability: You’re excited to explore new platforms, formats, creative approaches, and AI tools.
  • A detail oriented mindset: You’re organized, resourceful, and comfortable moving quickly from an idea to execution.
  • A portfolio or examples of on-camera or social-first content that demonstrate strong creative instincts and an understanding of what captures attention.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a fast-moving environment.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, Media, or a related field—or equivalent practical experience.

Why Aura?

  • Be part of a mission-driven company that's making a real difference in people's lives.
  • Work with a talented, passionate, and supportive team.
  • Real runway to pitch original ideas and drive content/social growth.

If you’re a thoughtful, social native who knows how to turn ideas into content that makes people hit follow—and you’re excited to make that your full-time focus—we encourage you to apply!

By proactively finding breakages, documenting issues, and prioritizing work across a 30+ person team, this role accelerates engineering velocity and product quality. The Impact you’ll make

AI Tool Operations Testing

Systems Process Optimization

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

Required:

  • Exceptional written communication for clear, structured bug reports and product feedback
  • Comfortable operating independently in ambiguous, fast-paced environments with minimal SOPs
  • Availability to work 40 hours/week, Monday–Friday, 9:00 am–5:00 pm Eastern Time (may shift slightly earlier after 3–4 weeks)

JOB TITLE: Contact Center Associate

Department: Contact Center

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt

Bilingual (English/Spanish) preferred

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are looking for a Contact Center Associate who is driven to make a positive impact on the employee and member experience. You are a strategic thinker with a bias for action. You have a relentless pursuit of excellence while bringing others along. You do not settle for mediocrity and are comfortable with challenging the status quo. If you’re always looking for more efficient and innovative ways of working, are thoughtful, intentional, and collaborative, we would love to talk to you!

The Contact Center Associate will provide friendly, effective and efficient service to membership over the phone and through all member channels while following the Credit Union policies, procedures, and guidelines. The Contact Center Associate, will support member inquiries in a people-driven attitude that drives an excellent member experience, including to properly refer more complex members inquiries to the appropriate channel. This is an exciting opportunity to bring forth new ideas and see those ideas come to life!

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

  • Answer calls or inquiries in a high-volume environment while providing excellent member service and meeting performance targets.
  • Contribute to and consistently meet departmental, individual, and organizational goals and targets; including service level standards, call metrics, quality of service, and production.
  • Proven expertise in credit union products and services, including card systems, wire transfers, online banking systems, and product referrals.
  • Uses sound judgement on when to engage support to resolve challenges, utilizing resources and training to answer inquiries.
  • Takes responsibility for quality and quantity of work.
  • Deliver expertise in credit union products and services, while assisting members with general inquiries, such as balances, transaction history, and stop payments.
  • Contribute to a strong Member Loyalty rating and after-call survey score by providing high quality service based on our service standards. Listening to our members, leading with empathy, owning the solution, delivering excellence, and utilizing appropriate escalation techniques.
  • Proactively perform tasks and contribute to member channel queues that directly impact member experience.
  • Manage all interactions with members, primarily over the phone, in a kind and welcoming manner that aligns to the mission and values of the credit union.
  • Lead with technology-based solutions and education to promote self-service, while finding creative solutions, problem solving, troubleshooting, and delivering on commitments.
  • Open to mentoring and coaching through review and analysis of real member transaction recordings in order to advance delivery of a premier level of service to our membership and community.
  • Responds positively to feedback and coaching.
  • Obtain a strong understanding of credit union products and services and refer them appropriately to members and potential members, and capture member feedback when appropriate.
  • Mitigate risk to the credit union by adhering to policies and procedures, including verification requirements, processing transactions with accuracy, and proactively identifying and escalating red flags.
  • Ability to support members and internal partners utilizing Seattle Credit Union services, including Online Banking, Mobile Apps, website, bill pay and ATM’s.
  • Maintain knowledge of Seattle Credit Union’s Bank Secrecy Act policy, procedures, and practices to meet compliance requirements, while keeping up to date on changes in policy and technologies.
  • Communicate effectively, both verbally and written, in English and a second language, if applicable.
  • Effectively adjusts to changing and evolving priorities and expectations.
  • Prepared to work during inclement weather or business continuity event, to ensure uninterrupted support for our membership. In addition, will be expected to find an private alternate location, if working remotely, if power or internet access is lost.
  • Demonstrated commitment to SCU Values.
  • Maintain reliable attendance and punctuality.
  • Other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU WILL BRING:

Basic Qualifications:

  • One (1)+ year of sales and/or retail service.
  • One (1)+ year high-volume call center experience.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Accurate 10-key, keyboarding/typing skills and at least a typing speed of 55 WPM.
  • Excellent telephone skills and communication skills.
  • Strong people and customer service skills, including ability to de-escalate.
  • Ability to connect with others with tact, discretion, and courtesy within and outside the organization.
  • Ability to perform basic math calculations.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities in a high-volume and fast-paced/multi-tasking environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Associate degree or higher.
  • One (1)+ year of experience in a financial institution, member-facing, high transaction role.
  • Experience handling chat, texting, or video interactions.
  • Experience with Fiserv systems, including DNA and Architect.

Working Conditions:

  • Work is primarily performed at an employee’s home office.
  • Requires all meetings to be on video and must be conducted in a private and professional manner.
  • Team members may attend special off-hour meetings and seminars.
  • The nature of work may include prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.

Benefits:

Seattle Credit Union supports and invests in our employees. We offer many great benefits, including low-cost medical contributions and zero contributions for dental and vision plans. Additionally, SCU offers a generous paid time off program and a 401k plan with a dollar-for-dollar employer to match up to 5%.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed above are representative of the knowledge, skills, and/or abilities required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Compensation is based on the candidate's geographical location, calculated based on an adjustment factor from Seattle area market compensation.

Why You’ll Love This Role

This is a people-first technical leadership role for someone who enjoys developing high-performing teams while staying close to the customer. You’ll lead and mentor the Solutions Engineering team supporting the Department of War (formerly DoD) and the Intelligence Community, setting clear standards for technical excellence, sales partnership, and execution. This team works in some of Cribl’s most complex and mission-critical environments – from enterprise SOCs to classified networks – alongside the channel and Federal Systems Integrator (FSI) partners who deliver with us.

You’ll have the opportunity to shape how pre-sales work gets done - reinforcing strong methodology, coaching consultative selling skills, and partnering closely with Sales leadership to drive meaningful revenue outcomes. You’ll balance strategy with hands-on leadership, supporting complex customer engagements while helping your team grow their technical depth and confidence.

As An Active Member Of Our Team, You Will ...

  • Lead the Department of War and Intelligence Community (DoW/IC) Solutions Engineering team, reinforcing sales methodology and metrics-led best practices

  • Build and leverage relationships across the channel and Federal Systems Integrator (FSI) community, partnering with Cribl’s Partner SE and Alliances teams so partners can land and expand Cribl within DoW and IC programs
  • Recruit, hire, and onboard SEs as the team grows, building a bench of mission-aware technical talent in the National Capital Region

  • Identify problem areas, formulate relevant solutions, and execute on them effectively.
  • We are a remote-first company, and work happens across many time zones – you may be required to perform duties outside your standard working hours occasionally

If You Got It - We Want It

  • Proven track record of successfully leading a technical pre-sales team or region at a software company, driving target attainment against monthly, quarterly, and annual quota targets
  • Background of successfully landing and expanding deals within the Department of War (DoD) and the Intelligence Community, including working through the channel and Federal Systems Integrator (FSI) communities
  • Ability to teach SEs how to identify new and existing opportunities through consultative selling methodologies
  • Experience in understanding and executing sales plays with an SE team, specifically land and expand plays, and tailoring those plays to drive revenue in your segment
  • Ability to communicate effectively in presentations with executive-level customers, direct reports, and the Cribl Leadership Team
  • Experience building technical champions within customers and prospects, including fostering relationships with senior executives and government and military leadership
  • Proven self-starter with a motivated attitude to be able to manage multiple tasks, projects, and responsibilities simultaneously
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines, while maintaining a pleasant and professional attitude towards your team, customers and co-workers
  • Working knowledge of the DoW/IC operating environment – classified and unclassified networks (e.g., NIPR, SIPR, JWICS), cross-domain considerations, FedRAMP and DoD Impact Level authorizations, and federal acquisition and budget cycles
  • Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent AND a minimum of 5 years of experience in pre-sales, preferably in a leadership capacity
  • Ability to travel up to 30%
  • Strong preference will be given to candidates with a background in selling Security, Observability, and/or data pipeline solutions (e.g., SIEM, log management, telemetry) into DoW and IC customers.
  • Active or prior U.S. security clearance is a plus, but not required.
  • Residence in the DC/VA/MD area.

We're looking for someone who takes ownership, is comfortable working with ambiguity, and uses AI responsibly to improve efficiency without compromising quality.

  • Review content regularly to remove outdated, duplicate, unclear, or missing information.

  • Gather requirements from stakeholders and create accurate content based on business needs.

  • Build and continuously improve the content creation and maintenance process across Support and Moderation.

Requirements

You will thrive if you have…

Must-haves

  • Strong English writing skills (C1+).

  • Experience in content writing, copywriting, knowledge management, content design, or similar.

  • Experience with Confluence or similar knowledge-base/documentation tools.

  • Experience using AI tools for writing, rewriting, summarising, structuring information, and content quality checks.

  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with high volumes of content and manage repetitive writing/editing tasks without losing quality.

  • Ability to adapt content for different audiences: support agents, moderation specialists, internal teams, and end customers.

  • Understanding of tone of voice and ability to adapt wording based on context, topic sensitivity, and audience.

  • Strong attention to detail, consistency, terminology, and structure.

  • Ability to organise information logically, identify duplicated, outdated, conflicting, unclear, or missing content, and maintain documentation so it is easy to find, use, and update.

Mindset and working style

  • Fast, practical, and execution-focused.

  • Comfortable working with large volumes of information.

  • Detail-oriented, but not perfectionistic.

  • Able to create a good version quickly, test it in practice, and improve based on feedback.

  • Understands digital users, online communication, and live entertainment context.

  • Supports company and team values in the way content is written and maintained.

  • Motivated by clarity, consistency, and usability.

  • Comfortable working remotely with a high level of ownership, transparency, and self-organisation.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience with Zendesk, Slack, chatbot tools, macro tools, or support platforms is a plus.

  • Experience in Support, Moderation, Customer Operations, or similar is a plus.

  • Experience with Jira, Asana, Monday, Notion, or other task/request management tools.

Conditions

  • Competitive compensation with a service contract.

raw.description:
TÉRMINOS DE REFERENCIA

CONSULTORÍA PARA EL DESARROLLO DE UNA METODOLOGÍA DE FORMACIÓN DE FORMADORES SOBRE EL PROTOCOLO PARA LA INVESTIGACIÓN Y JUZGAMIENTO DE CASOS DE VIOLENCIA SEXUAL EN OAXACA

Título de la consultoría: Desarrollo de una metodología de formación de formadores sobre el Protocolo para la investigación y juzgamiento de casos de violencia sexual en Oaxaca, México

Unidad organizativa: Programas

Reporta a: Representante Regional para ALC y Associate Manager, ​Advocacy LAC

Ubicación: Remoto

Idiomas: Español

Fecha límite de solicitud: 2 de octubre de 2026

Duración: finales de octubre - finales de febrero

Honorarios de la consultoría: Fase 1: $3,000; Fase 2: $2,500 USD

SOBRE EQUALITY NOW:

Equality Now es una organización global de derechos humanos dedicada a lograr los cambios legales y sistémicos necesarios para poner fin a la discriminación contra todas las mujeres y niñas, en todo el mundo. Desde su fundación en 1992, ha contribuido a la reforma de 140 leyes discriminatorias a nivel global, impactando positivamente en la vida de cientos de millones de mujeres y niñas, así como en sus comunidades y países, tanto en el presente como para las generaciones futuras.

Trabajando con aliadas y aliados a nivel nacional, regional y global, Equality Now combina una profunda experiencia jurídica con una diversidad de perspectivas sociales, políticas y culturales para seguir liderando, orientando e impulsando los cambios necesarios para alcanzar una igualdad de género duradera, en beneficio de todas las personas. Para más información sobre Equality Now, visita.

OBJETIVOS:

Diseñar una metodología híbrida de Formación de Formadores (FdF) para aplicar el Protocolo para la investigación y juzgamiento de casos de violencia sexual, con enfoques de género, derechos humanos e interculturalidad. La metodología fortalecerá las capacidades de las personas operadoras de justicia de Oaxaca para replicar y adaptar la formación de manera autónoma y sostenible, mediante espacios de formación cruzada con otros actores clave.

ENTREGABLES:

Producto 1. Documento metodológico de Formación de Formadores

Propuesta pedagógica y operativa para formar a personas operadoras de justicia de Oaxaca en el Protocolo para la investigación y juzgamiento de casos de violencia sexual, con una duración de 16 a 24 horas en modalidad presencial, síncrona o asíncrona.

El documento incluirá objetivos y competencias; perfiles de participantes y personas formadoras; módulos, contenidos y actividades; criterios éticos y de autocuidado; evaluación del aprendizaje; seguimiento de la aplicación y réplica del Protocolo; y criterios para el pilotaje, validación y ajuste de la metodología.

La propuesta deberá contemplar tres componentes articulados:

  • Componente teórico-conceptual: apropiación y aplicación práctica de los contenidos técnicos y jurídicos del Protocolo, con énfasis en los estándares de derechos humanos y su aplicación en la investigación y juzgamiento de casos de violencia sexual.
  • Componente metodológico-pedagógico: desarrollo de competencias para la enseñanza de personas adultas en el ámbito jurídico, incluyendo estrategia de facilitación, uso de los recursos pedagógicos y manejo de situaciones que puedan surgir durante la formación.
  • Componente

    práctico

    de

    microenseñanza: ejercicios de simulación en los que los participantes pongan en práctica la facilitación de contenidos y actividades, con retroalimentación y evaluación de sus competencias técnicas y pedagógicas.

Producto 2. Caja de herramientas pedagógicas para la Formación de Formadores

Materiales editables y accesibles para implementar y replicar la formación, incluidos guías de facilitación, presentaciones, ejercicios, casos prácticos e instrumentos de evaluación, según corresponda.

Los materiales deberán facilitar la aplicación del Protocolo con enfoques de género, derechos humanos, interculturalidad e interseccionalidad, y criterios de confidencialidad y no revictimización. La caja de herramientas y el documento metodológico se ajustarán durante el pilotaje para entregar sus versiones finales.

Producto 3. Validación y pilotaje progresivo de la metodología y la Caja de Herramientas para la Formación de Formadores (ToT)

La persona consultora implementará, por etapas, un pilotaje de la Formación de Formadores con personas operadoras de justicia de Oaxaca, en coordinación con Equality Now y conforme al cronograma acordado. Equality Now facilitará el componente técnico y jurídico; la persona consultora estará a cargo de los componentes metodológicos, pedagógico y prácticos.

Durante el pilotaje, la persona consultora deberá:

  • Poner a prueba la metodología y los materiales desarrollados en los Productos 1 y 2.
  • Facilitar ejercicios de aplicación y microenseñanza para que las personas participantes practiquen cómo replicar la formación.
  • Observar y valorar sus competencias de facilitación mediante criterios definidos previamente.
  • Recoger y sistematizar la retroalimentación sobre la claridad, pertinencia y utilidad de la metodología y los materiales.
  • Identificar e incorporar los ajustes necesarios para facilitar la implementación y réplica de la formación.

Entregables:

  1. Informe breve de pilotaje y validación con los resultados, la retroalimentación recibida, las fortalezas y áreas de mejora identificadas, los ajustes realizados y las recomendaciones para futuras réplicas. La persona consultora presentará el informe en una reunión con el equipo de ALC.
  2. Versión final validada del documento metodológico y de la caja de herramientas, con los ajustes derivados del pilotaje y lista para su implementación y réplica.

La consultoría se llevará a cabo en dos fases:

Fase 1

octubre-diciembre 2026

  • Productos 1 y 2
  • Revisión y retroalimentación

Fase 2

Enero–febrero 2027

  • Validación del componente metodológico-pedagógico
  • Validación del componente práctico
  • Revisión y retroalimentación.
  • Versión final de la metodología y Caja de Herramientas para las formaciones híbridas/online.

El orden de los contenidos en este calendario está sujeto a modificación según las recomendaciones de la persona consultora.

PERFIL Y CUALIFICACIONES DE LA PERSONA CONSULTORA:

Formación académica y capacidades

  • Formación universitaria en ciencias jurídicas, ciencias sociales, educación, estudios de género, derechos humanos o áreas afines. Se valorará la formación especializada acreditada en violencia sexual, acceso a la justicia, derechos humanos, perspectiva de género, interculturalidad o educación de personas adultas.
  • Capacidad para analizar y sintetizar contenidos jurídicos y técnicos complejos y comunicarlos de forma clara, accesible y no discriminatoria.
  • Capacidad para trabajar de manera autónoma, organizar el trabajo, coordinarse con equipos interdisciplinarios y cumplir con los productos y plazos establecidos en los TDR.

Experiencia y conocimientos técnicos

  • Al menos cinco años de experiencia profesional relevante en derechos humanos, igualdad de género, acceso a la justicia o reparación, particularmente en relación con la violencia basada en género o la violencia sexual.
  • Experiencia en el diseño, desarrollo y evaluación de procesos de Formación de Formadores (FdF) dirigidos a personas adultas, preferentemente a personas operadoras de justicia, al funcionariado público u a otros actores institucionales. Los procesos deberán contemplar la transferencia de conocimientos y el desarrollo de competencias para que las personas participantes puedan replicar la formación.
  • Experiencia en diseño instruccional y en metodologías de aprendizaje para personas adultas, con enfoques participativos y orientados a la aplicación práctica. Se valorará el uso de casos, simulaciones, ejercicios participativos y otras metodologías activas, en modalidades presenciales, virtuales o híbridas.
  • Experiencia en la elaboración de guías metodológicas, manuales, currículos, cajas de herramientas y otros materiales técnicos y pedagógicos que faciliten la implementación y la réplica de procesos formativos, con un lenguaje claro, accesible y no discriminatorio.
  • Conocimiento y aplicación de estándares nacionales e internacionales de derechos humanos relacionados con la violencia basada en género y la violencia sexual, en particular en materia de igualdad y no discriminación, debida diligencia, acceso a la justicia, derechos de niñas, niños, adolescentes y mujeres, protección de víctimas y sobrevivientes, y reparación integral.
  • Conocimiento del funcionamiento de los sistemas de procuración e impartición de justicia en casos de violencia sexual y violencia basada en género, incluidos los procesos de investigación y juzgamiento, los estándares probatorios, la actuación de las instituciones competentes y las medidas para prevenir la revictimización. Se valorará especialmente la experiencia en el diseño, la implementación o la evaluación de protocolos, herramientas o capacitaciones dirigidos a personas operadoras de justicia.
  • Experiencia en la facilitación de procesos formativos y de espacios de intercambio entre distintos actores, incluidas instituciones públicas, fiscalías, poderes judiciales, organizaciones de mujeres y de la sociedad civil, y personas defensoras de derechos humanos. Deberá demostrar capacidad para conducir procesos participativos y abordar con cuidado situaciones sensibles relacionadas con la violencia sexual y las experiencias de victimización.
  • Experiencia en la incorporación de enfoques de género, derechos humanos e interculturalidad en procesos pedagógicos, adaptando los contenidos y las metodologías a los contextos, perfiles y necesidades de las personas participantes.

Conocimientos y experiencia deseable en el contexto de Oaxaca

Se valorará especialmente que la persona consultora cuente con:

  • Conocimiento del contexto sociocultural y territorial de Oaxaca, en particular de las condiciones y barreras que afectan el acceso a la justicia de mujeres, niñas y adolescentes sobrevivientes de violencia sexual.
  • Conocimiento de los sistemas normativos indígenas y comunitarios, así como de las dinámicas de articulación entre estos sistemas y el sistema estatal de justicia, desde un enfoque de derechos humanos e interculturalidad.

POSTULACIÓN:

Las personas interesadas deberán presentar:

  • Una breve carta de presentación en la que describan su experiencia relevante para la consultoría e incluyan enlaces a ejemplos de metodologías o materiales pedagógicos que hayan desarrollado.
  • Un cronograma de trabajo propuesto, que indique las principales actividades, etapas y tiempos previstos para el desarrollo de los productos, incluyendo los momentos de coordinación, validación y pilotaje.
  • Un currículum vitae (CV) que acredite la formación y la experiencia señaladas en el perfil requerido.
Salary: Fase 1: $3,000; Fase 2: $2,500 USD

raw.description:
Build the Practice. Scale the Teams. Partner with Growth-Stage Operators.
In 2008, Propeller reinvented the way venture-stage companies build finance teams, and in the process we defined the category the market now calls fractional. Three years ago, we quietly began building what comes next, expanding to serve our breakout clients as they scaled past venture and brought leadership in-house. That became our Growth practice: today it serves our largest clients and generates a third of Propeller's revenue. Now, with the practice staged to break out, we're hiring the leader who will professionalize and scale it.
You'll own the practice end to end: its commercial engine, its embedded delivery teams, and the strategic relationships that anchor it, bringing the horsepower Growth-stage Consumer companies need as they scale from $30M to $300M and beyond.
Growth-stage companies operate differently than venture-stage startups. The financial infrastructure is more complex. The operational stakes are higher. The boards are more demanding. The margin for error is smaller as companies approach exit velocity. And turnover in the finance seat stays high, because these companies accelerate faster than even exceptional talent can adapt. These clients need a CFO partner who has lived the $30M-to-$300M journey; someone who knows where the landmines are, how to build the systems that scale, and who has the career experience and confidence to make the case for uncomfortable truths when a situation requires it.
This is an equity-track leadership role for someone ready to build a practice, not just a portfolio.

Who We ARE
Today, Propeller's 250+ professionals serve as the embedded finance and accounting partner to some of the most iconic emerging companies in Consumer, Technology, Blockchain, and Business Services. All are full-time employees, across three continents; none are contractors or freelancers. Behind us: 1,500+ companies served, $105B+ in enterprise value created, 26 unicorn alumni, and $29B+ raised. Ahead of us: the transformation of professional services through AI-enabled intelligence.
Our embedded teams integrate seamlessly into client operations in multi-year partnerships. We attend weekly leadership meetings, participate in board prep, collaborate on strategic decisions, and have direct access to client CEOs and CFOs. This embedded positioning creates trust, access, and influence that traditional providers never achieve.
PropellerOS, our financial operating platform, combines human judgment, precision accounting, data infrastructure, and AI-enabled insight to transform finance from a back-office function into the central nervous system of growth. The system enables finance-grade standards of lineage, reconciliation, auditability, and explainability, with a named human accountable for every number we ship.

Key Responsibilities

Most leadership roles emphasize one dimension. This role requires three.
At $30M to $300M there is no bench to delegate to, so the finance leader architects the data systems, engineers the process change, and directs the AI that now carries the mechanical work, all at once. The market treats each of those as its own job. We built the infrastructure that makes them one: embedded access, AI fluency training, and dedicated change-management capacity behind every engagement.

Commercial Leader
You own the Growth practice's expansion: pipeline, bookings, retention, and P&L. You think like a business owner. You build relationships before you need them, identify opportunities others miss, and close deals that grow the practice. You develop go-to-market strategy for Growth-stage Consumer companies and build the private equity, investor and advisor relationships that generate referrals. Sixty-seven percent of our closed-won new business comes from referrals, so the network already produces; your job is to point it at Growth and extend it. If you wait for business development to hand you leads, this isn't your role.

Service Leader
You build the teams that carry our Growth portfolios: Controllers who each run their own client book. Controller and CFO are parallel tracks here, not rungs on one ladder, and part of your job is placement, putting people in the seat where their strengths compound. A brilliant controller running five clients flawlessly outranks a miscast CFO in every way that matters to a client. You set service standards and hold people accountable for client satisfaction, deliverable quality, and engagement profitability. You know that excellence at scale requires systems, not heroics. You conduct regular portfolio reviews, build capacity through hiring and development, and step in when engagements need senior attention. If you need to do everything yourself or avoid difficult management conversations, this isn't your role.

Strategic Partner
You serve as CFO-level advisor to Growth-stage Consumer operators, bringing the pattern recognition that only someone who has scaled companies from $30M to $300M can offer. You maintain strategic relationships with the most complex clients in the segment. You walk into boardrooms and command respect, translate financial data into strategic insight, and deliver difficult messages with clarity. You know where companies break as they grow: the systems that stop working, the hires that become urgent, the board dynamics that shift. The exposure compounds, too: across the portfolio you'll sit in more boardrooms in a quarter than most operating CFOs see in a year. And when an AI-produced analysis goes to a board, you are the one who certifies it and stands behind it in the room. If your experience is primarily early-stage or primarily enterprise, this isn't your role.
  • Drive business development through networking, referrals, strategic partnerships, and direct outreach.
  • Own financial performance of the Growth practice: revenue, margins, utilization, and profitability.
  • Lead and develop the practice's embedded teams, placing people in the seats where their strengths compound.
  • Serve as executive sponsor and escalation point for key accounts.
  • Participate in board meetings and investor conversations for strategic clients.
  • Make informed decisions about pricing, resource allocation, and engagement scope.
  • Use PropellerOS to deliver the cross-client insight no single-company CFO can access, and codify what works at Growth stage back into it so your judgment compounds for every client in the practice.
  • Continuously improve service delivery quality, efficiency, and client impact across the practice.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

  • Demonstrated business development success: ability to identify, cultivate, and close client relationships in coordination with our GoToMarket team.
  • 15+ years in finance/accounting with at least 7 years in CFO or senior financial leadership roles.
  • Direct experience scaling companies from $30M to $300M+ in revenue, ideally as CFO or VP Finance.
  • Demonstrated AI fluency: you work with AI in your own finance workflow today, and you can walk us through how it changes what you produce.
  • Track record leading and developing teams: managing managers, not just individual contributors.
  • Multi-client or consulting background strongly preferred (Big 4, boutique advisory, PE portfolio, or similar).
  • Strong executive presence; comfortable presenting to boards, private equity sponsors, and sophisticated stakeholders.
  • Experience building financial infrastructure that scales: ERP transitions, reporting systems, planning processes.

Industry Expertise
You understand how Consumer businesses work: the economics, the channels, the metrics, the seasonal rhythms, the retail relationships, the brand dynamics. Deep expertise in at least one of: DTC/e-commerce (CAC, LTV, channel economics, fulfillment optimization, Shopify/Amazon ecosystem); CPG (trade spend, retailer margins, inventory turns, COGS optimization, promotional ROI); or omnichannel retail (wholesale vs. DTC mix, sell-through rates, gross margin management, supply chain finance) along with experience in core processes and systems, such as inventory, trade spend, Quickbooks, Netsuite, etc. Business Services depth alongside Consumer is a plus.

Job Benefits

Job Title: Practice Leader, Growth
Location: Remote-flexible with occasional travel

DEI Statement: At Propeller Industries, we encourage our employees and our clients to bring their true selves to the organization. We believe that a diverse team enables us to cultivate and improve upon our culture of inclusion and collaboration. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome the contributions that you can bring in terms of your education, opinions, culture, ethnicity, race, sex, gender identity and expression, nation of origin, age, languages spoken, veteran’s status, religion, disability, sexual orientation, and beliefs. So however you identify and whatever your background, we encourage you to apply for this role if you share our passion for helping great entrepreneurs build great companies. We look forward to meeting you!

Compensation
  • Base salary range $300,000 - $350,000 + significant variable compensation tied to practice performance and new business.
  • Equity participation.
  • Investment in your development: AI/automation training, executive coaching, and access to Propeller's network.
  • Remote-flexible with travel for client meetings, team leadership, and conferences

Current Benefits Offered: Generous Paid Time Off and Holiday pay, Comprehensive health benefits plus dental, vision, short and long-term disability, and life insurance. HSA contribution, Paid Family Leave, 401k match and Remote Work. We also help you grow in your professional life.

raw.description:
Technical Project Manager - MSP / IT Infrastructure

Remote - United States
$90,000-$95,000 + Benefits
Travel to Southern California / Los Angeles County for initial training and approximately 1-2 company visits per year

We are recruiting for a Technical Project Manager opportunity with an established managed IT services company that has been serving small and midsized businesses for more than 25 years.

This is a remote position focused on leading the successful delivery of IT infrastructure and software implementation projects across multiple client environments.

This is not a traditional non-technical project management position.

The ideal candidate will come from an MSP background and combine strong project leadership skills with significant hands-on infrastructure experience. You should be comfortable planning and coordinating projects while also understanding the underlying technology well enough to lead technical discussions, troubleshoot issues and perform implementation work when necessary.

This could be an excellent opportunity for an experienced MSP Project Engineer, Senior Systems Engineer or Infrastructure Engineer who has already been leading projects and is ready to move into a dedicated Technical Project Manager role.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own assigned IT projects from approved scope through planning, implementation, testing, documentation and final handoff

  • Translate scopes of work into detailed project plans with tasks, owners, dependencies, milestones, estimated effort and completion criteria

  • Manage multiple concurrent projects across different client environments

  • Lead infrastructure projects including server installations and upgrades, Active Directory migrations, Microsoft 365 implementations, Azure projects, virtualization projects, network upgrades, firewall deployments, workstation rollouts and disaster recovery initiatives

  • Coordinate technicians, engineers, vendors, client contacts and internal stakeholders throughout each project

  • Lead project kickoffs, technical working sessions, status meetings and completion reviews

  • Validate technical prerequisites including equipment, licensing, backups, access, documentation, maintenance windows and rollback plans

  • Track project scope, schedules, budgeted effort, dependencies, risks and resource requirements

  • Identify potential problems early and escalate technical or project-related blockers before they impact delivery

  • Provide hands-on technical implementation and troubleshooting when necessary

  • Perform structured testing and quality assurance before projects are considered complete

  • Maintain accurate technical and project documentation including configurations, diagrams, credentials, decisions, changes and test results

  • Ensure completed projects are handed off cleanly to ongoing support teams

  • Participate in post-project reviews and help improve project delivery processes

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience working for a Managed Service Provider (MSP)

  • Significant experience leading multiple concurrent IT infrastructure projects across different client environments

  • Strong hands-on Windows Server administration experience including server deployment and configuration

  • Strong Active Directory and Group Policy experience including domain controller deployment and domain administration

  • Strong Microsoft Azure administration experience

  • Strong networking experience including routers, switches, VLANs and firewalls

  • Experience configuring and deploying firewalls

  • Experience with virtualization technologies including Hyper-V and/or VMware ESXi

  • Experience with Microsoft 365 environments and migrations

  • Ability to take an approved scope of work and independently turn it into an organized, executable project plan

  • Strong understanding of project scheduling, resource coordination, risk management, change control, testing, documentation and operational handoff

  • Ability to coordinate technical resources effectively without necessarily having direct supervisory authority

  • Strong troubleshooting skills and the ability to make sound technical decisions during project implementation

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

  • Strong organizational and time-management skills

  • Ability to work independently with minimal oversight

Nice to Have

Experience with any of the following is helpful but not required:

  • HaloPSA

  • Kaseya

  • NinjaOne

  • Hudu

  • IT Glue

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This company has built an unusually stable team and client base over more than 25 years in business. They place a strong emphasis on employee retention, work-life balance, professional development and giving experienced employees the autonomy to do their jobs without constant micromanagement.

Additional highlights include:

  • Remote work

  • Very low employee turnover

  • Long-term client relationships

  • Mature processes, procedures and documentation

  • Dedicated 24/7/365 technical coverage, so this position is not the first responder for routine after-hours or holiday support incidents

  • Strong Help Desk and Support Desk teams

  • Significant autonomy and minimal micromanagement

  • Career development and advancement opportunities

  • Comprehensive benefits

Compensation and Location

The salary range for this position is $90,000-$95,000, depending on experience, plus a comprehensive benefits package.

This position can be performed remotely from anywhere in the United States.

Candidates must be willing and able to travel to Southern California / Los Angeles County for initial training and approximately 1-2 times per year thereafter for company meetings or other business needs.

If you are an experienced MSP infrastructure professional who enjoys owning projects, coordinating resources and seeing technical implementations through from planning to successful completion, we would like to hear from you.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

We are a boutique IT recruiting agency that strictly works with IT consulting companies and managed services providers. We place candidates on a permanent, full time basis (no contract or contract-to-hire positions).

Requirements

Join us and build a €1B+ company with us!

raw.title: Mobile Developer (React Native)
raw.excerpt: Digital Forms is a consulting-led digital transformation firm, founded in Warsaw in 2015 and now 70+ people strong.
raw.description:
Digital Forms is a consulting-led digital transformation firm, founded in Warsaw in 2015 and now 70+ people strong. We work with mid-market and enterprise clients across Europe, the UK, and the US — helping them turn operational complexity into measurable business outcomes. We started as a mobile development shop. Over ten years, we built something different: a firm where every product is grounded in a real business case, and where engineering quality is as important as strategy. Our team is fully remote, our clients are international, and our standards are high.

This role sits at the heart of that delivery.

As Senior Mobile Developer, you will be embedded in a high-stakes client engagement - building a greenfield mobile app for a premium international luxury retail brand, from the first architectural decision to launch.

The role and responsibilities:

We are building a brand-new iOS and Android app — from scratch — as part of a major digital transformation for a premium international luxury retail brand. The app will serve 250k+ daily active users across global markets from the moment it launches.

The product replaces static navigation with a dynamic, content-driven Feed ecosystem: personalised brand stories, exclusive offers, and live in-store updates, delivered with the engagement depth of social media. It is a greenfield project — no legacy code, no technical debt, full architectural ownership from day one. The app goes live in Q3.

As Senior Mobile Developer, you will own the architecture and delivery of the app end to end. You will write code every day — this is a pure hands-on engineering role, with no team management responsibility. The client expects senior autonomy from the start. You will work alongside a senior cross-functional team: backend engineers, frontend web developers, UI/UX designers, and a PM.

Architecture & technical leadership

  • Architect from scratch: Design the React Native app structure, patterns, and coding standards that the entire project will build on.

  • Define the content model: Work alongside FE Web developers to design the mobile content model powering dynamic, segmented delivery.

  • Drive technical decisions: Own integration choices for CMS, DAM, and personalisation tooling — and be able to defend them.

Feature development & integrations

  • Integrate CMS, DAM & personalisation: Connect the tooling that delivers the right content to the right user — context-aware, segmented, and real-time.

  • Implement deep linking: Build campaign-tied navigation flows and personalised user journeys across iOS and Android.

  • Ship push notifications: Design and implement the full push notification layer, including deep links and campaign landing flows.

  • Collaborate on features: Build and maintain new features together with backend engineers; work with UI/UX designers to assess feasibility and deliver high-quality UX.

Performance & quality

  • Optimise for scale: Own caching strategy, content-fetching architecture, and rendering performance for an app used by hundreds of thousands of people daily.

  • Instrument analytics: Implement event tracking that supports personalisation decisions, A/B testing, and experimentation.

  • Write quality code: Idiomatic, well-tested React Native — unit and component coverage as standard practice.

  • Own distribution: Manage iOS and Android release cycles and store submissions.

Requirements

Must-have:

  • React Native — 5+ years of professional experience building production iOS and Android apps from scratch.

  • iOS and Android platforms — both, including distribution cycles, store submissions, and platform-specific behaviour.

  • CMS & DAM integration — hands-on experience delivering dynamic, segmented content in mobile via headless CMS and DAM tooling.

  • Personalisation & experimentation platforms — integrating decisioning tools, recommendation engines, or A/B testing systems into a live mobile product.

  • Deep linking — production experience implementing campaign and personalised navigation flows.

  • Push notifications — full implementation including deep links and campaign flows.

  • REST API integration — connecting mobile apps to backend services at production scale.

  • Performance optimisation — caching, content-fetching, and rendering strategies for personalised, high-traffic apps.

  • Analytics & event tracking — instrumentation supporting personalisation and product experimentation.

  • Testable code — appropriate unit and component test coverage as standard practice.

  • English C1+ — written and spoken; direct communication with an international client team is a hard requirement.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with streaming APIs or AI-assisted feature integration.

  • App analytics platforms such as Firebase or Amplitude.

  • Consent management and third-party privacy tooling (GDPR).

  • Mapping SDKs — Google Maps, Mapbox, or similar.

  • Automated testing beyond unit and component level (E2E, integration).

  • Broader JS ecosystem: , React, .

  • A/B testing, feature flagging, and mobile attribution.

  • Headless CMS architectures in retail or e-commerce environments.

  • Understanding of UI/UX design principles and ability to assess feasibility.

  • Polish is a plus; all project communication is conducted in English.

Highlights

Build a brand-new mobile app for a premium luxury retail brand, used by 250k+ daily users.

Own the full architecture — React Native, CMS, DAM, personalisation — from day one.

raw.description:
Join the company that’s building the telemetry infrastructure for the AI era. At Cribl, we partner with IT and Security teams at many of the world’s biggest enterprises, including half of the Fortune 100, to bridge the gap between AI ambition and infrastructure reality. As the AI Platform for Telemetry, we give customers the choice, control, and flexibility to manage and analyze telemetry for both humans and agents, so they can build what’s next.

We’re one of the fastest‑growing private companies and a leading player in a massive, fast‑moving market. With a global workforce, we’re remote‑first and grounded in a simple idea: software is a people business. Cribl is the place where curious, collaborative people can do their best work, grow fast, and bring their full selves to the herd.

This is a remote role based in Washington, DC

Why You’ll Love This Role

This is a people-first technical leadership role for someone who enjoys developing high-performing teams while staying close to the customer. You’ll lead and mentor the Solutions Engineering team supporting the Department of War (formerly DoD) and the Intelligence Community, setting clear standards for technical excellence, sales partnership, and execution. This team works in some of Cribl’s most complex and mission-critical environments – from enterprise SOCs to classified networks – alongside the channel and Federal Systems Integrator (FSI) partners who deliver with us.

You’ll have the opportunity to shape how pre-sales work gets done - reinforcing strong methodology, coaching consultative selling skills, and partnering closely with Sales leadership to drive meaningful revenue outcomes. You’ll balance strategy with hands-on leadership, supporting complex customer engagements while helping your team grow their technical depth and confidence.

As An Active Member Of Our Team, You Will ...

  • Lead the Department of War and Intelligence Community (DoW/IC) Solutions Engineering team, reinforcing sales methodology and metrics-led best practices
  • Provide ongoing mentorship to SEs on pre-sales techniques for securing new clients and expanding within existing customers, across our full portfolio of solutions
  • Continually assess and develop the technical capabilities of each team member to ensure each SE reaches and maintains the required technical knowledge to perform their pre-sales duties effectively
  • Provide periodic performance reviews, assess skill sets, coach through performance and personnel matters, and create personal/professional development opportunities
  • Partner with the DoW and IC Regional Sales Directors and their Regional Sales Managers, aligning SE coverage, sales plays, and campaigns to achieve revenue targets
  • As the technical leader for DoW/IC, deliver customer presentations, present technical information about Cribl’s products and services, conduct product demonstrations, and oversee SE-led Proof of Value events, including in classified and air-gapped environments when required
  • Build and leverage relationships across the channel and Federal Systems Integrator (FSI) community, partnering with Cribl’s Partner SE and Alliances teams so partners can land and expand Cribl within DoW and IC programs
  • Recruit, hire, and onboard SEs as the team grows, building a bench of mission-aware technical talent in the National Capital Region
  • Stay current on the DoW/IC mission, budget, and acquisition landscape – contract vehicles, FedRAMP and DoD Impact Level authorizations, Zero Trust and federal logging mandates – and translate it into how the team positions Cribl
  • Identify problem areas, formulate relevant solutions, and execute on them effectively.
  • We are a remote-first company, and work happens across many time zones – you may be required to perform duties outside your standard working hours occasionally

If You Got It - We Want It

  • Proven track record of successfully leading a technical pre-sales team or region at a software company, driving target attainment against monthly, quarterly, and annual quota targets
  • Background of successfully landing and expanding deals within the Department of War (DoD) and the Intelligence Community, including working through the channel and Federal Systems Integrator (FSI) communities
  • Ability to teach SEs how to identify new and existing opportunities through consultative selling methodologies
  • Experience in understanding and executing sales plays with an SE team, specifically land and expand plays, and tailoring those plays to drive revenue in your segment
  • Ability to communicate effectively in presentations with executive-level customers, direct reports, and the Cribl Leadership Team
  • Experience building technical champions within customers and prospects, including fostering relationships with senior executives and government and military leadership
  • Proven self-starter with a motivated attitude to be able to manage multiple tasks, projects, and responsibilities simultaneously
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines, while maintaining a pleasant and professional attitude towards your team, customers and co-workers
  • Working knowledge of the DoW/IC operating environment – classified and unclassified networks (e.g., NIPR, SIPR, JWICS), cross-domain considerations, FedRAMP and DoD Impact Level authorizations, and federal acquisition and budget cycles
  • Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent AND a minimum of 5 years of experience in pre-sales, preferably in a leadership capacity
  • Ability to travel up to 30%
  • Strong preference will be given to candidates with a background in selling Security, Observability, and/or data pipeline solutions (e.g., SIEM, log management, telemetry) into DoW and IC customers.
  • Active or prior U.S. security clearance is a plus, but not required.
  • Residence in the DC/VA/MD area.

The salary for this role is dependent on geographic location and will be based on the individual candidate's job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

In addition to base salary, for sales and some sales-adjacent roles, employees are eligible to earn incentive compensation (commission). For all other roles, employees are eligible to participate in the Cribl Corporate Bonus Program.

In addition to a competitive salary, Cribl also offers a generous benefits package which includes health, dental, vision, short-term disability, and life insurance, paid holidays and paid time off, a fertility treatment benefit, 401(k), and equity.

Base Salary Range
$168,000—$200,000 USD

Bring Your Whole Self
Diversity drives innovation, enables better decisions to support our customers, and inspires change for the better. We’re building a culture where differences are valued and welcomed, and we work together to bring out the best in each other. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or any other applicable legally protected characteristics in the location in which the candidate is applying.
